Property.name: RegexFileFilter
Property.Description: Regex pattern to filter which files are processed. Only files that match the File Spec AND the RegexFileFilter will be processed. To use only the Regex Filter, set File Spec to *. To use only the File Spec, set RegexFileFilter to blank.

Property.name: SuccessEmailSubject
Property.Description: This is the subject to use on the success email Email Identifier - "%f-FileName,%CD-CurrentDate,%CT-CurrentTime, %Q-Timestamp using normal Ensemble format"

Property.name: SucessEmailBody
Property.Description: Email This is the body that will be included in the success email Email Identifier - "%f-FileName,%CD-CurrentDate,%CT-CurrentTime, %Q-Timestamp using normal Ensemble format"

Property.name: FailureEmailSubject
Property.Description: This is the subject to use on the failure email Email Identifier - "%f-FileName,%CD-CurrentDate,%CT-CurrentTime, %Q-Timestamp using normal Ensemble format"

Property.name: FailureEmailBody
Property.Description: Email This is the body that will be included in the failure email Email Identifier - "%f-FileName,%CD-CurrentDate,%CT-CurrentTime, %Q-Timestamp using normal Ensemble format"

Property.name: ActionOnSourceFile
Property.Description:
This is the action to be taken on the SOURCE file.

If the source file is to be left as is leave this field blank, but be aware this leaves the possibility the file will be processed again.

If you want to delete the source file from the server, enter DELETE (this replaces the original DeleteFromServer function).

If the source file needs to be renamed but remain in the current folder on the server, just enter the new name.

If the file needs to be moved to a new folder on the source server, include the full absolute path to the new location including the new file name.

NOTE: The following special values can also be included in the new file names:
%f - The original filename of the file
%CD - The date the file was processed in format 1970-01-01
%CT - The time the file was processed in format 12:00:00AM
%# - The current sequence number

EXAMPLE: Setting this value to %f_%CD_%CT_%# would rename testfile to something like

testfile_08/07/2015_02:39:23PM_1

Property.name: valueToBeReplaced
Property.Description: Property to store the values to be replaced

Property.name: Filename
Property.Description:
Name of file to output the document(s) to. May include timestamp specifiers. The %f specifier if present will be replaced with the name of the document's original source filename (stripped of characters illegal in target filenames).

See the method Ens.Util.File.CreateTimestamp() for documentation of timestamping options.

Property.name: TargetConfigNames
Property.Description: Configuration item(s) to which to send file stream messages

Property.name: StartingSequenceNumber
Property.Description: This is the value the sequence number is set to each time the component is restarted, assuming ResetSequenceOnRestart is set to true

Property.name: MinimumSequenceNumber
Property.Description: This is the lowest value the sequence number can have. If the sequence number is below this value and the SequenceIncrement is less than zero, the sequence number is reset to the MaximumSequenceNumber. If the sequence number is less than the MinimumSequenceNumber and the SequenceIncrement is greater than zero, the sequence number is set to the MinimumSequenceNumber. If MinimumSequenceNumber is set to be more than the MaximumSequenceNumber, the sequence number will be set to zero.

Property.name: MaximumSequenceNumber
Property.Description: This is the highest value the sequence number can have. If the sequence number is above this value and the SequenceIncrement is greater than zero, the sequence number is reset to the MinimumSequenceNumber. If the sequence number is higher than the MaximumSequenceNumber and the SequenceIncrement is less than zero, the sequence number is set to the MaximumSequenceNumber. If MaximumSequenceNumber is set to be less than the MinimumSequenceNumber, the sequence number will be set to zero.

Property.name: SequenceIncrement
Property.Description: This is how much we add to the sequence number every time we get a new event. This value can be set negative, which will result in a descending sequence number. If this value is set to zero, the sequence number will not change.

Property.name: ResetSequenceOnRestart
Property.Description: Determines whether or not we reset the sequence number when we restart this business service

Property.name: JournalIncomingData
Property.Description: Determines whether or not we journal data as it is received (before other processing)

Property.name: JournalOutgoingData
Property.Description: Determines whether or not we journal data as it is sent (after other processing)

Parameter.name: CONTAINERCLASS
Parameter.Description: Setting the Target Config Names as part of the configuration

Method.name: OnInit
Method.Implementation:
$$$TRACE("OnInit")
Set ..MinimumSequenceNumber=$ZSTRIP(..MinimumSequenceNumber,"<>W") $$$TRACE("Current Minimum Sequence Number is "_..MinimumSequenceNumber) Set ..MaximumSequenceNumber=$ZSTRIP(..MaximumSequenceNumber,"<>W") $$$TRACE("Current Maximum Sequence Number is "_..MaximumSequenceNumber)
do ..ResetSequenceNumber()
Quit $$$OK

Method.name: OnProcessInput
replaceWithParticularFormat
Method.Implementation:
Set key = "" For { Set ReplaceVal = ..valueToBeReplaced.GetNext(.key) Quit:key="" Set SubBody = $REPLACE(SubBody,key,ReplaceVal)
} $$$TRACE("Done with replacement; SubBody="_SubBody) Quit SubBody

Method.name: ResetSequenceNumber
VerifySequenceNumber
IncrementSequenceNumber
Method.Implementation:
Set PreIncrementedSequenceNumber = ^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber") Set ^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber") = ^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber") + ..SequenceIncrement
$$$TRACE("Sequence Number has been incremented from "_PreIncrementedSequenceNumber_" to "_^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber"))
Do ..VerifySequenceNumber()
